### This is a living document.
:::

**WISE-APP** *Weather Impact Simulation and Evaluation for Adaptation Policy and Planning* is a tool designed to estimate potential welfare outcomes under different weather conditions before events occur.

It quantifies the relationship between weather and welfare, simulates outcomes under historical and future climate scenarios, and evaluates the impact of various adaptation policies.

This user guide walks you through all key features and steps to use WISE-APP effectively.

## Limitations

WISE-APP results reflect observed **statistical reslationships**, they are not grounded in *causal impact evaluations* and do not represent forecasts. The model estimates the relationship between local variation in weather conditions and outcomes of interest — typically household welfare, conditional on other factors.

Key limitations:

- **No tail-risk events** The data and models do not capture extreme rare events.
- **Direct impacts only.** Indirect effects of weather such as spillovers and market effects are not estimated.
- **Data- and assumption-dependent.** Results are sensitive to the quality and variability of the underlying data and to the assumptions made in modelling.

## How to access WISE-APP

[WISE-APP online](https://datanalytics-int.worldbank.org/wise-app){target="_blank"}

- This option requires World Bank single sign-on credentials.

[WISE-APP R package](https://github.com/worldbank/welfare-weather-app){target="_blank"}

- This option requires R and access to [WISE-APP data](data.qmd).
- To install and run locally:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("worldbank/welfare-weather-app")
wiseapp::run_app()
```
:::


## This guide

This guide covers the data that underpins WISE-APP and the three analysis steps:

- [**Data**](data.qmd) — Household survey and weather data: sources, structure, and coverage.
- [**Model Welfare**](step1.qmd) — Establish the statistical relationship between weather and outcomes of interest. The fitted model is the foundation for all subsequent steps.
- [**Climate and Weather Scenarios**](step2.qmd) — Apply the fitted model to historical and future climate scenarios to produce a distribution of weather-driven outcomes.
- [**Policy Scenarios**](step3.qmd) — Re-simulate outcomes under counterfactual policy interventions (social protection, infrastructure, digital access, labour market) to quantify direct welfare gains and changes in climate resilience.

## Data

WISE-APP connects to a data directory containing household survey microdata and weather data. The data are spatially linked using the H3 indexing system. For more details, see the [Data section](data.qmd) of this guide.

- The [welfare-weather-app-data](https://github.com/worldbank/welfare-weather-app-data) repository contains the code used to prepare data for WISE-APP.

## Getting help

If you encounter any issues or have questions, please [open an issue](https://github.com/worldbank/welfare-weather-app-docs/issues) on the GitHub repository.
